kaps_punt: Nasionale simbole sedert 1994: Landswapen, Nasionale vlag, Volkslied

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het in 1994 ná baie jare van stryd teen apartheid 'n demokrasie geword.
items.bron: The Presidency (thepresidency.gov.za/node/6133): 27 April 1994 was the first democratic election, ending apartheid rule; SAHO 27 April 1994 (sahistory.org.za/node/13157).

items.bewering: Die nuwe simbole moes toe vir almal geld en nie net vir sommige nie.
items.bron: gov.za national coat of arms page: the motto calls for unity in diversity and a common sense of belonging; gov.za flag page: the design reads as the convergence of diverse elements of society. The intent of inclusive symbols is officially stated.

items.bewering: Die nasionale vlag is in 1994 aanvaar, en die staatsheraldikus Fred Brownell het die ontwerp gemaak.
items.bron: gov.za/about-sa/national-symbols/national-flag: first used 27 April 1994, designed by former State Herald Fred Brownell; Wikipedia 'Frederick Brownell': State Herald 1982-2002; University of Pretoria tribute (up.ac.za). Proclamation of 20 April 1994 per SAHO dated event.

items.bewering: 'n Groen band soos 'n Y oor die vlag loop. Die Y se twee arms begin in die boonste en onderste hoek langs die vlagpaal. Hulle kom in die middel van die vlag saam. Daarvandaan loop hulle as een band reguit na die buitenste kant toe.
items.bron: gov.za national flag page: the design begins at the flagpost in a 'V' form and flows into a single horizontal band to the outer edge of the fly. The Y comparison maps correctly: the lesson spells out that the arms start at the hoist corners and the stem runs to the fly, so a learner is not left with an upright Y.

items.bewering: Die amptelike beskrywing sê hierdie vorm kan gelees word as verskillende dele van die samelewing. Daardie dele kom bymekaar en gaan dan saam vorentoe.
items.bron: gov.za national flag page: 'can be interpreted as the convergence of diverse elements within South African society, taking the road ahead in unity.'

items.bewering: Die kleure op die vlag het geen amptelike betekenis nie. Die regering se eie beskrywing sê mense heg verskillende betekenisse aan die kleure. Daarom behoort niemand een gedeelde betekenis aan 'n kleur te koppel nie.
items.blok: Die kleure het geen amptelike betekenis nie
items.bron: gov.za national flag page: 'Individual colours, or colour combinations represent different meanings for different people' and 'no universal symbolism should be attached to any of the colours.'

items.bewering: Die nuwe landswapen is op 27 April 2000 aanvaar, en daardie dag is Vryheidsdag.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: gov.za national coat of arms page (adopted on Freedom Day, 27 April 2000); Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa': introduced on Freedom Day, 27 April 2000.

items.bewering: Die wapen het baie dele, en elkeen dra sy eie betekenis.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: gov.za national coat of arms page lists each element with its meaning; dws.gov.za coat of arms page likewise.

items.bewering: 'n Sekretarisvoël hou sy vlerke gelig, en die voël staan vir groei en beskerming.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: gov.za national coat of arms page: uplifted wings, symbol of growth and speed and of protection of the nation against its enemies; Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa': raised wings represent the nation's ascent while offering protection. The lesson's pair is two of the several officially stated meanings.

items.bewering: 'n Protea staan vir die skoonheid van die land en vir ons vermoë as 'n nasie.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa' and gov.za: 'an emblem of the beauty of our land' and the flowering of our potential as a nation. 'Vermoë' renders 'potential' loosely but not falsely.

items.bewering: 'n Opkomende son beteken helderheid en die belofte van 'n nuwe begin.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa': the sun is 'an emblem of brightness, splendour' and symbolises rebirth; gov.za coat of arms page: the promise of new beginnings.

items.bewering: Twee mensfigure op die skild groet mekaar, en daardie groet beteken eenheid.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa': the figures 'are depicted facing one another in greeting and in unity'; gov.za coat of arms page; sahistory.org.za/article/national-coat-arms.

items.bewering: Albei kom van een figuur in die San se rotskuns op die Lintonsteen. Die wapen se ontwerp het die spieëlbeeld daarvan bygevoeg en so die groet gemaak.
items.blok: Vier van die landswapen se dele
items.bron: The Conversation, 'Rock art: how South Africa's coat of arms got to feature an ancient San painting' (theconversation.com/...-195297, also on wits.ac.za, Rock Art Research Institute): 'The two human figures come from one painting of a male figure. He's been mirrored and stylised to form a gesture of greeting.' Wikipedia: figures derived from Khoisan rock art on the Linton Stone.

items.bewering: Die wapen se leuse is !ke e: /xarra //ke. Dit lyk na 'n fout, maar die tekens is deel van die spelling en nie leestekens nie.
items.bron: gov.za coat of arms page gives the motto in this form; Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa' writes it 'ǃke e꞉ ǀxarra ǁke' with click letters (ǃ, ǀ, ǁ) and a length mark, i.e. letters of the orthography, not punctuation; Wikipedia 'ǀXam language' on the click letters.

items.bewering: Die woorde kom uit die taal van die ǀXam-mense, een van die Khoisantale.
items.bron: gov.za coat of arms page: 'written in the Khoisan language of the /Xam people'; Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa'.

items.bewering: Niemand praat daardie taal vandag nog as moedertaal nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'ǀXam language' and 'List of extinct languages of Africa': extinct, last known speakers died in the 1910s; STIAS (stias.ac.za/2020/04/rediscovering-a-khoisan-language).

items.bewering: Die leuse beteken letterlik dat verskillende mense saamkom.
items.bron: gov.za coat of arms page: 'literally means: diverse people unite'; Wikipedia word-for-word gloss 'people who are different meet'.

items.bewering: Die volkslied is een korter lied wat uit twee ou liedere saamgestel is.
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page and SAHO (sahistory.org.za/article/national-anthem): 'a shortened, combined version of Nkosi Sikelel iAfrika and The Call of South Africa'.

items.bewering: Enoch Sontonga het Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika in 1897 geskryf, en hy was 'n onderwyser by 'n sendingskool.
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page and SAHO: 'composed in 1897 by Enoch Sontonga, a Methodist mission school teacher.'

items.bewering: Die Stem van Suid-Afrika was eers 'n gedig wat Langenhoven in Mei 1918 geskryf het.
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page: 'Die Stem van Suid-Afrika is a poem written by CJ Langenhoven in May 1918.'

items.bewering: Die dominee De Villiers het in 1921 die musiek daarvoor gemaak.
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page: 'The music was composed by the Reverend ML de Villiers in 1921.'

items.bewering: Die laaste strofe is in Engels, en daardie woorde is nuut geskryf. Hulle is nie 'n vertaling van die lied se Afrikaanse strofe nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'National anthem of South Africa': 'The new English lyrics were adapted from the last four lines of the first stanza of Die Stem van Suid-Afrika (English: The Call of South Africa)', with changes 'to reflect hope in post-apartheid South African society'. SAHO and gov.za: the official English version, The Call of South Africa, was accepted in 1952. The second sentence is true, because the English lines come from a different part of Die Stem than the Afrikaans stanza sung today. The first is not: the English words were adapted from Die Stem's older English version, not written from nothing.
items.regstelling: Keep that the English stanza is not a translation of the Afrikaans stanza sung in the anthem, but drop 'nuut geskryf'. Correct: in 1997 the English words were adapted from another part of Die Stem's older official English version (The Call of South Africa) and changed to fit the new country. Watch the next sentence, about people who used to sing their own songs: once this is fixed, the block must not imply that the English stanza has no link to Die Stem.

items.bewering: Mense wat vroeër elk hulle eie lied gesing het, sing nou een lied saam.
items.bron: SAHO and gov.za national anthem pages: two separate songs with separate histories (Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika first sung publicly in 1899; Die Stem sung on official occasions from 1928 and the sole national anthem 1957-1994, per Wikipedia 'Die Stem van Suid-Afrika') were combined into one anthem in 1997. A general statement, defensible at this level.

items.bewering: Die lied word in vyf tale gesing, en die eerste strofe alleen bevat twee daarvan.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'National anthem of South Africa': Xhosa (first stanza, first two lines), Zulu (first stanza, last two lines), Sesotho, Afrikaans, English, which makes five; gov.za national anthem page.

items.bewering: Eerste strofe: isiXhosa en isiZulu deel dit / Tweede strofe: Sesotho / Derde strofe: Afrikaans / Laaste strofe: Engels
items.blok: Die tale, in die volgorde waarin hulle gesing word
items.bron: Wikipedia 'National anthem of South Africa' (stanza languages and order as listed); gov.za national anthem page (official text in this order).

items.bewering: Die vlag het eerste gekom en is in 1994 aanvaar.
items.blok: Drie van die land se simbole, drie jare
items.bron: gov.za national flag page (first used 27 April 1994). Note: the 20 April 1994 proclamation also made the two old songs a dual anthem (SAHO dated event; Wikipedia), so 'eerste' holds only for the CURRENT forms of the three symbols. The block says so itself ('sy huidige vorm', and the two songs between 1994 and 1997), so read in context the order is correct.

items.bewering: Die volkslied het sy huidige vorm op 10 Oktober 1997 gekry.
items.blok: Drie van die land se simbole, drie jare
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page and SAHO: proclamation in Government Gazette No. 18341, dated 10 October 1997; Wikipedia: published in the Government Gazette on 10 October 1997.

items.bewering: Tussen 1994 en 1997 het die land twee liedere as volkslied gehad, en mense het hulle ná mekaar gesing.
items.blok: Drie van die land se simbole, drie jare
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page and SAHO: the 20 April 1994 proclamation gave the Republic two national anthems; Wikipedia: both were performed at Mandela's inauguration, and 'performing both of them took as much as five minutes', which made the arrangement cumbersome.

items.bewering: Die landswapen het laaste gekom en is eers in 2000 aanvaar.
items.blok: Drie van die land se simbole, drie jare
items.bron: gov.za coat of arms page and Wikipedia: introduced 27 April 2000, after the flag (1994) and the anthem's current form (1997).

items.bewering: Die ou landswapen van 1910 het dus ses jaar lank in 'n demokrasie bly staan.
items.blok: Drie van die land se simbole, drie jare
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa': granted by royal warrant on 17 September 1910; the 2000 arms replaced 'the earlier national arms, which had been in use since 1910'. The 1930 and 1932 versions in use until 2000 are described as renditions of those arms, so 'van 1910' holds. 27 April 1994 to 27 April 2000 is six years.

items.bewering: Die land het ook ander simbole, soos die nasionale blom.
items.blok: Drie van die land se simbole, drie jare
items.bron: Brand South Africa, 'South Africa's national symbols' (brandsouthafrica.com) lists the national flower, the king protea, among the national symbols; SANBI (pza.sanbi.org/node/10828).

items.bewering: simbool: Iets wat mense sien of hoor en wat vir hulle iets meer beteken as homself.
items.bron: The standard sense of 'simbool' / 'symbol' (a thing that stands for something beyond itself) fits every use in this lesson (flag, coat of arms, anthem). The gov.za national symbols pages use the term this way.

items.bewering: landswapen: Die amptelike teken van 'n land, met dele wat elkeen iets beteken.
items.bron: gov.za national coat of arms page: the coat of arms is the highest visual symbol of the state, and each element has a stated meaning.

items.bewering: staatsheraldikus: Die amptenaar wat amptelike tekens en wapens opteken en met die ontwerp daarvan help. Hy doen dit ook vir dorpe, skole en ander groepe, nie net vir die land nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Bureau of Heraldry': registers arms, badges, flags and seals and keeps the public register, and 'Anyone ... may apply to register arms'; Wikipedia 'South African heraldry': it registers civic and corporate arms as well as official and personal arms; SAVA via qz.com: Brownell as State Herald 'designed and oversaw the development of numerous coats of arms, badges and flags'. Schools are not named in these sources but are covered by 'anyone'.

items.bewering: sekretarisvoël: 'n Groot grys roofvoël wat op die grond jag en lang pote het.
items.bron: National Geographic 'Secretary birds' and Britannica 'secretary bird': a large raptor, about 1.2-1.3 m tall, that hunts on foot, with long crane-like legs and light grey body plumage (black flight feathers and thighs).

items.bewering: protea: Protea is die naam van baie soorte blomme wat in Suid-Afrika groei. Een van hulle, die koningprotea, is Suid-Afrika se nasionale blom.
items.bron: SANBI PlantZAfrica, Protea cynaroides (pza.sanbi.org/node/10828): the king protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus has more than 92 species, subspecies and varieties; Wikipedia 'Protea cynaroides'.

items.bewering: leuse: 'n Kort spreuk wat sê waarvoor 'n land of 'n groep staan.
items.bron: Matches the standard meaning of 'motto' and how gov.za describes the national motto (a phrase that calls the nation to unity in diversity).

items.bewering: rotskuns: Prente wat mense lank gelede op klip gemaak het.
items.bron: Scientific American, 'Rock Art in Southern Africa': images painted or engraved on rock surfaces, made over thousands of years; SAHO uKhahlamba-Drakensberg Park page. 'Prente ... gemaak' covers both paintings and engravings.

items.bewering: Lintonsteen: Die klip met ou rotskuns waar die landswapen se twee figure vandaan kom. Albei kom van een figuur daarop: die wapen se ontwerp het die spieëlbeeld daarvan bygevoeg en so die groet gemaak.
items.bron: The Conversation / Wits Rock Art Research Institute (theconversation.com/...-195297): one male figure from the Linton panel, mirrored and stylised into a greeting; Wikipedia 'Coat of arms of South Africa'; sahistory.org.za/article/national-coat-arms (the Linton stone is in the South African Museum, Cape Town).

items.bewering: spieëlbeeld: Die beeld wat jy in 'n spieël sien, met links en regs omgeruil.
items.bron: The standard meaning of mirror image (left-right reversed). It fits the coat-of-arms use in The Conversation's account ('mirrored').

items.bewering: volkslied: Die amptelike lied van 'n land, wat by groot geleenthede gesing word.
items.bron: gov.za national anthem page: the anthem is the official national song, proclaimed in the Government Gazette; SAHO: Die Stem was sung on official occasions from 1928.

items.bewering: strofe: 'n Groep reëls wat saam een deel van 'n lied vorm.
items.bron: The standard meaning of stanza/strofe; Wikipedia 'National anthem of South Africa' uses 'stanza' in exactly this sense for the anthem's parts.

items.bewering: sendingskool: 'n Skool wat lank gelede deur 'n kerk begin is.
items.bron: The Heritage Portal, 'The contested but pivotal legacy of missionary education in South Africa' (theheritageportal.co.za); SAHO Hermannsburg School and Mission Museum: mission schools were run by Christian missions, that is churches and missionary societies, rather than by the state. In this lesson the word describes the 1890s, so 'lank gelede' fits.

opsomming: One sentence is false: the lesson says the English stanza of the anthem was newly written, but in 1997 its words were adapted from another part of Die Stem's old English version. That it is not a translation of the Afrikaans stanza is right and should stay. Everything else checked out, including the dates, the flag's shape and the official reading of its colours, the coat of arms' parts, and the mirrored Linton figure.
